quote: I now have a brand new roof,
stewart_read: Customer clears the prior roof-age DQ herself and volunteers it — a strong qualifying/enthusiasm signal the rep should reflect back to reinforce readiness.
coaching_implication: Rep should have said something like 'that's great, that clears the roof concern from before' to reinforce progress instead of letting it pass silently into the next line.

quote: then I had my AI go over it. And found AI found some things I didn't care for, so I ended up canceling.
stewart_read: A rich disclosure about why a signed contract was cancelled goes completely unprobed — rep moves straight to the interest question.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be strategically avoiding re-litigating a competitor's contract to keep the call moving toward booking, but the missed detail (outside-power restriction) directly threatens Ion's own contract later.
coaching_implication: Ask 'what did the AI flag specifically?' — that answer (generator/outside-power clause) is exactly the kind of term the closer needs pre-loaded.

quote: Because I signed it and everything, then have my AI go over it and the AI is screaming.
stewart_read: Second touch on the same AI-vetting behavior; rep's only response is a filler acknowledgment.
coaching_implication: This is the second of three touches — flag to closer explicitly rather than letting it repeat unaddressed.

quote: I'm running the contract through my AI.
stewart_read: Third and final touch, stated as a closing condition on the appointment itself — customer is telling the rep the deal is contingent on passing this scrutiny.
coaching_implication: This belongs directly in the handoff brief as a named condition, not folded into small talk.

quote: I need a battery backup system for just my boiler.
stewart_read: A specific, well-defined technical need is handed to the rep and filed silently — no reflection, no forward hook ('the specialist can size exactly that for you').
coaching_implication: Reflect specific asks back as forward-pulling hooks: 'got it — boiler backup, not the big whole-home battery — I'll flag that so the specialist sizes it right.'

quote: and so then you can just upload a photo of that bar graph onto there. Is this a good number to send a text message to?
stewart_read: Rep gets the bill photo but never states or confirms an actual dollar amount or flips it into urgency — capture without anchor.
coaching_implication: After the photo lands, rep should ask 'and roughly what's that running you a month?' to convert the document into a spoken pain point.

quote: I am not trying to be told what I can and cannot do on my property for the next twenty five years.
stewart_read: This is the customer naming the exact contract-term fear that killed her last deal — a live objection precursor the rep never reframes or reassures against.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be intentionally not engaging to avoid sounding like she's overselling contract terms she can't speak to at setter level.
coaching_implication: A brief reassurance ('that's a fair concern — our consultant will walk through exactly what's allowed') would have closed the anxiety loop instead of leaving it open into the appointment.
